## What The Business Is

Applied Materials (AMAT) is a Santa Clara–based semiconductor manufacturing equipment and services company. Its core business is selling materials-engineering systems, software and support used by chipmakers and display manufacturers; as of its latest reporting structure, its two reportable segments are **Semiconductor Systems** and **Applied Global Services (AGS)**. ([appliedmaterials.com](https://www.appliedmaterials.com/us/en/about.html?utm_source=openai))

## What It Does

AMAT’s Semiconductor Systems business supplies tools for critical wafer-fab and packaging process steps, including deposition, etch, rapid thermal processing, chemical mechanical planarization, metrology/inspection, wafer packaging and ion implantation. AGS monetizes the installed base through spares, services, upgrades and software intended to improve ramp speed, equipment performance, fab output and cost. ([companiesmarketcap.com](https://companiesmarketcap.com/applied-materials/sec-reports-10k/0001628280-25-056742/?utm_source=openai))

Strategically, management is positioning AMAT around AI-driven semiconductor demand, especially **leading-edge foundry/logic**, **DRAM/HBM**, and **advanced packaging**. In the May 14, 2026 earnings-call excerpt, management said these areas are its “sweet spot,” expected them to drive more than 80% of year-on-year wafer-fab-equipment growth in 2026, and highlighted 8-quarter visibility from large customers.

- **Record fiscal Q2 2026 results and stronger guide:** AMAT reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of **$7.91B**, non-GAAP gross margin of **50.0%**, non-GAAP operating margin of **32.1%**, and non-GAAP EPS of **$2.86**; it guided Q3 revenue to **$8.95B ± $500M** and non-GAAP EPS to **$3.36 ± $0.20**. ([ir.appliedmaterials.com](https://ir.appliedmaterials.com/news-releases/news-release-details/applied-materials-announces-second-quarter-2026-results?utm_source=openai))

- **AI-driven demand visibility improved:** In the May earnings script, management said demand signals strengthened across leading indicators, customers were providing rolling 8-quarter forecasts, and AMAT now expected its semiconductor equipment business to grow **more than 30%** in calendar 2026. ([investors.appliedmaterials.com](https://investors.appliedmaterials.com/static-files/28ef7eff-8b4d-418e-999a-dbfa403ce6f3?utm_source=openai))

- **New product cadence in high-value areas:** On April 8, AMAT introduced deposition systems for angstrom-era logic/GAA chips, including Trillium ALD and a selective nitride PECVD system; on June 25, it introduced new systems for DRAM and advanced packaging, including epitaxy, CMP, deposition and eBeam offerings aimed at HBM, 3D stacking and AI chip architectures. ([ir.appliedmaterials.com](https://ir.appliedmaterials.com/news-releases/news-release-details/applied-materials-introduces-deposition-systems-angstrom-era/?utm_source=openai))

- **Advanced packaging expansion:** On May 3, AMAT agreed to acquire ASMPT’s NEXX business, a supplier of large-area advanced-packaging deposition equipment, strengthening AMAT’s panel-level packaging portfolio for larger AI accelerator packages. ([ir.appliedmaterials.com](https://ir.appliedmaterials.com/news-releases/news-release-details/applied-materials-broadens-advanced-packaging-portfolio?utm_source=openai))

## Bull Case
- AI-driven WFE cycle is accelerating: management guided semiconductor equipment business to grow **>30% in CY2026**, with 8-quarter demand visibility from leading foundry/logic, HBM/DRAM and advanced packaging customers.
- Record Q2 FY2026 ($7.91B revenue, 50% GM, $2.86 EPS) and a Q3 guide of $8.95B implies ~$34–36B annualized revenue run-rate, well above the $29.0B TTM.
- TTM FCF ($5.34B) is depressed vs. net income ($8.51B) due to working-capital build ahead of the ramp; FCF conversion should normalize toward net income, implying forward FCF of $8B+.
- NEXX acquisition, angstrom-era deposition products, and EPIC ecosystem (TSMC partner) reinforce share gains in the highest-growth WFE segments.

## Bear Case
- Valuation is extreme: current EV/FCF is ~82x (FCF/EV of 1.2%) vs. a 3-yr average FCF yield of ~4.1%, implying the multiple must more than halve to revert to historical norms.
- Market cap has run to ~$440B vs. a 3-yr mean of ~$179B — a highly momentum-driven level with 42% historical volatility.
- China/export-control risk is live: $253M BIS settlement in Q2, plus ongoing tariff/licensing uncertainty that could dent China revenue and gross margins.
- WFE is cyclical; any AI capex digestion in 2027 could compress both estimates and the multiple simultaneously.

1. **Forward FCF:** TTM FCF of $5,343M understates earnings power (TTM net income $8,508M) due to inventory/receivables build into the ramp.
